headline: At seed 17 and a 10-second configured solver budget, CPSolver/UniTime won all 21 feasibility-first comparisons: it produced an officially feasible schedule on all 21 ITC-2007 curriculum instances, while Planora did so on 17, and it had a lower official objective on all 17 common-feasible instances.
claim_boundary: This is a counterbalanced, full-corpus breadth gate with one disclosed seed, not a replicated statistical study. It rejects a Planora-superiority claim at this configuration. It does not establish performance at other seeds, budgets, hardware, solver versions, or non-ITC problem families.

protocol.execution_order: Planora ran first on comp01 and every odd-numbered instance; CPSolver ran first on comp02 and every even-numbered instance.

validation.no_output_note: The official validator was invoked for every produced .out file. The four Planora NO_SOLUTION cases created no .out file and therefore had no validator invocation.

paired_result.ranking_rule: Feasibility first, then lower official ITC-2007 objective.

timing.accounting_definition: wall_time_seconds and cpu_time_seconds measure each fresh solver subprocess from launch to exit and exclude the later official-validator subprocess. Planora worker_* fields measure inside the fresh Python worker after interpreter and module startup. CPU seconds are child user plus system CPU from RUSAGE_CHILDREN.
timing.budget_note: Both solvers received the same 10-second configured algorithm budget, one worker, seed 17, and CPU 0. CPSolver launch-to-exit wall time includes JVM startup. Planora launch-to-exit wall time includes Python/import/conversion startup and is materially above its internal worker time.

failure_analysis.observed_behavior: Each NO_SOLUTION case used only the approximately 3-second initial partitioned feasibility slice, returned UNKNOWN, and did not consume the remaining approximately 7 seconds of the configured budget.
failure_analysis.highest_value_next_gate: Retain or construct a fast incumbent across the full budget: continue feasibility search with a monolithic or alternative partitioned fallback when the first slice returns UNKNOWN, then start official-objective LNS only after a validated incumbent exists.
failure_analysis.quality_gap_signal: On the 17 common-feasible instances, Planora's largest aggregate weighted-component disparity is room capacity: 3592 versus 116. This supports prioritizing capacity-aware room assignment and incumbent construction before further bandit tuning.

verdict.supported_statement: Under this single-seed, 10-second, one-worker, CPU-pinned ITC-2007 breadth protocol, CPSolver/UniTime achieved 21/21 official feasibility and won all 21 feasibility-first comparisons; it had a lower official score on all 17 common-feasible instances, while Planora produced no solution on the other four.
verdict.research_interpretation: The candidate adaptive seeding remains a positive comp01 engineering ablation, but the external breadth result shows that incumbent construction, feasibility-budget allocation, and room-capacity optimization dominate the current cross-solver gap.
